name: 🥖 Philly Cheesesteaks
tagline: Thin-shaved ribeye, sweet onions and melty cheese, piled into toasted rolls.

items.name: Ketchup or hot peppers, to serve

steps.text: Freeze the ribeye 30–40 minutes so it firms up, then slice it as thin as you can against the grain.
Cook the onions (and pepper) in butter and a little oil over medium until soft and sweet. Set aside.
Split the rolls, not all the way through, and toast them cut side down in the pan.
Turn the heat to high. Add oil, then the steak in one layer. Season with salt and pepper; sear 1 minute, then chop and toss with a spatula until just cooked.
Mix the onions back in and divide into 4 piles. Lay 2 slices of cheese on each pile and let it melt, 30 seconds.
Put a roll face down over each pile, slide the spatula under and flip it into the roll.

kid_jobs.job: Lay the cheese slices on the piles
Set out ketchup, hot peppers and pickles

chef_tip: Partly freeze the ribeye before slicing. It's the only way to get paper-thin shavings at home, and thin is what makes it a real cheesesteak.
make_ahead: Slice the steak in the morning and fridge it; cook the onions ahead too.
leftovers: Best fresh. Leftover meat and onions make a great cheesesteak quesadilla.
swaps: Provolone or Cheez Whiz instead of American
heads_up: Ribeye into the freezer 30–40 minutes before slicing.
